correctness.rationale: Reassessed the complete corrected RESULT.md in repairs/2/. The exact original extremal theorem survives. The original decimal equality ended in …495 rather than the actual prefix …4962; the original proof also referred to one nonzero centered eigenvalue when α=0, at which the centered operator is zero. The replacement corrects the decimal, states rank at most one with eigenvalue zero at independence, and makes the exponent-zero convention explicit. For an exact decimal certificate bracket s_0 by the rationals 0.78615137775742328606 and 0.78615137775742328608: the polynomial (2s²+1)²−5 has opposite signs there. Evaluation at those rationals and decreasing B_1 put the coefficient strictly between 0.075055351553114962 and 0.075055351553114963. For the theorem, the margins and groundedness hold by substitution. For α=−t∈(−1,0), the factor u(2−tu) is increasing; the mixed density is everywhere nonnegative exactly if 1−t(2−t)²=(1−t)(t²−3t+1)≥0, yielding t≤r. For α≥0 the density is positive; α≤−1 fails by collapse or an interior pole. Writing c−1=αg(u)g(v), with g=f′ and f=u(1−u)/(1+αu), gives ∫g=0 and ∫g²=1/[3(1+α)] by direct integration of (1+αu)^{-2} and (1+αu)^{-4}, including α=0 by continuity. The unimodal f peaks at u*=1/(1+s), so ∫|g|=2/(1+s)². These identities yield p_m and the half-L¹ formula B_m. To obtain the past–future coefficient attach the conditional past given U_0 and the conditional future given U_m separately to the endpoints using the Markov property. This cannot increase TV; projection from full paths to the endpoints gives the reverse inequality. On the negative branch the strict maximum is s_0, and the log derivative 2[m−(s−1)²]/[s(s²−1)] gives the unique positive-branch maximum 1+√m. The lag-one negative endpoint beats B_1(2) by the stated exact upper rational bracket on s_0. For m≥2, independently checked B_2(39/50)<1/54 and (1−s_0²)/(3s_0²)<1/4, so even the benchmark B_m(2) beats the entire negative branch. The asymptotic follows from the prefactor ∼2/m and (1−(1+√m)^{−2})^{m−1}→e^{−1}. The centered eigenvalue formula gives |α/[3(1+α)]|^m as maximal correlation, including zero at independence, with the distinct large-positive-α limit stated in the record.
